notes.title: Sales, Sales, Sales! and Announcement on Development
notes.content:
[u][b]Hi everyone! It has been far too long.
[/b][/u]

Let me start off by apologizing for the lack of involvement and interaction in the game dev space. I have been stuck in some fairly aggressive schooling for the past 2 years (CPA Designation…) which has been taking up quite a bit of time. As a result, I have not been able to pump out my goal of 2 games per year, nor have I been able to spend much time, passion and energy in the development of any games in general.

I am happy to say that my final exam in next week (Wednesday to Friday – yes… a 3 day long final exam ☹) and after that, I am pleased to say that I can jump into the world of development once again!!

[u][b]Go forward projects:[/b][/u]

I have recently published Night at the Office (Late 2024) which is more of the traditional TurnVex style game.

My favorite game and my most advanced game is Snafu. Snafu has been an absolute blast to develop and is extremely unique. The reception the game has received is fantastic. Unfortunately, the spotlight out in the frontlines has been limited to the point where it’s fallen into the shadows quite fast. It’s unfortunate, but reality.

My goal for 2025 (and perhaps early 2026) is to develop the next Snafu with a focus on MMO style (without the online component). This approach is a big step up from what I am most comfortable with, but I believe it will be a fun project to work on. Similar to Snafu, it is not the traditional spooky house approach that most horror games are, but rather a unique approach that rarely ever sees the light of day. It may see the same fate as Snafu, falling out of the light quite fast, but it will be a blast to develop!

As always, I want to thank all my followers and those who have supported the journey of developing horror games! I look forward to jumping back into work within the next coming weeks to begin pumping out some spooky games to you all.

With that being said, to commemorate the end (hopefully…) of schooling, finally… All of my games will be 75% off for the week. 

Cheers! And happy gaming, everybody.

Stan. T

notes.title: Night at the Office - New Horror Game - Out This Friday
notes.content:
Happy December, everyone.

Just wanted to let you all know that my next horror game Night at the Office is now officially complete and is ready for launch this Friday the 13th. 

It's been a real pleasure developing Night at the Office, but there definitely were some challenges along the way.

It's been nearly two years since I've released a game, and that is mainly due to both work and school eating up a significant piece of 2023 and 2024, so it was a little difficult getting back into the slow stages of development, especially after releasing Snafu, which I believe to be one of my greatest concoctions. The bar was set quite high, in my opinion...

Nonetheless, Night at the Office takes a traditional approach which I have done in the past, however, with a bit more focus on story and puzzle aspects of the game.

It is always an honour to be able to build these games and push out what lingers in the imagination into a actual playable product; so to that, as always, I hope you all enjoy what Night at the Office has to offer when it releases this coming Friday. And if you could leave a review, providing me with your thoughts on what you enjoyed and/or disliked about the experience, I would greatly appreciate that!

Cheers, everybody and happy gaming.

notes.title: Is Simon There? is coming tomorrow!
notes.content:
Hello, everybody. I hope you are all doing very well.

I wanted to let you all know that my latest horror Is [u][b]Simon There?[/b][/u] will be releasing tomorrow at 10am PST / 11am Mountain time.

[u][b]Is Simon There?[/b][/u] will be slightly different from some of my more recent releases (i.e. Within Skerry and Inside Depth 6) in that it will focus primarily on creating an atmosphere for the player to dive into. 

[u][b]Is Simon There?[/b][/u] will have fewer [b]required puzzles[/b] (excluding optional puzzles) and fewer "aimless, eventless wandering". My goal is to tell a story while keeping you on the edge of your seat, while anticipating the next event to happen. 

Of course, like my previous games,[u] [b]Is Simon There?[/b][/u] will include 3 endings and 1 Easter Egg/ special ending. I've toned the difficulty of these optional puzzles down a little so that the vast majority of players can experience all the game has to offer without relying on too many guides. 

AND finally, no more getting knocked-out black screens. Nothing but silky smooth progression, a dark story, a neat little Easter Egg, and a hand full of intuitive puzzles to keep you thinking, throughout the 40 minute long journey. 

[u][b]Once again, Is Simon There? will be releasing tomorrow (May 06, 2022). And as always, if you play the game, please leave an honest review. I would love to know what you enjoyed and disliked about the game. [/b][/u]

Once [u][b]Is Simon There?[/b][/u] has been published, I will be spending some time researching new mechanics / systems to implement into new games (i.e. controller support, advanced AI, potential VR, etc)

Cheers, everybody!

Stan. T

notes.title: Within Skerry - New upcoming terror
notes.content:
After several months of development, I am happy to finally announce Within Skerry - my new horror game which is aiming to be my scariest game to date.

It has been a long journey. From learning new mechanics, introducing new elements of horror, and trying to find the perfect balance between suspense and scares; it was definitely a long journey with many road blocks. However, after overcoming these roadblocks, and after settling in to new full-time work in accounting, I am happy to announce that Within Skerry is 80% complete in development.

In terms of completion, all that remains is creating an ending, bonus content, and hell-of-a-lot of polishing / testing. Normally this would not take too long; however, with me working full-time again, a significant amount of development time has been cut. Nonetheless, my aim is to release a Steam page in early January, and HOPEFULLY release the entirety of Within Skerry in early February.

With me luck, everybody!

p.s. Within Skerry will be playable with several new subtitle languages - English, Russian, Polish, Korean, and Japanese. This will be my first time dabbing in foreign languages, so wish me luck in that, too, I guess! :)

Please enjoy some screenshots of Within Skerry.

Stan. T

notes.title: Inside Depth 6 - Version 2.0 is here!
notes.content:
Hello everybody, and happy Wednesday!

I wanted to let you all know that Inside Depth 6 version 2.0 is now available. With version 2 comes an entire new area to explore ([b]Hell hole[/b]) which also offers as an alternative route to Depth 4. This serves very well for replayablility purposes, allowing you to take differing paths for each playthrough. Hell Hole offers approximately 8-10 min of new content and fright!

[b]Here is a list of all changes and fixes completed in version 2.0 of Inside Depth 6: 
[/b]
- [New Content] - Hell Hole (Alternative route to Depth 4 at the bottom of Depth 3).
- [New Content] - Minor additions to existing game (Triggers and assets),
- [Update] - Unity Engine updated to version 2020.3.2.
- [Fixes] - Added multiple safeguards to prevent the very unlucky few from falling through the map. Safeguards will teleport player back into a certain area of their current depth.
- [Fixes] - Beginning date subtitles changed to reflect actual story timeline. 
- [Fixes] - Removed the ability to climb up the Depth 3 world tree.
- [Fixes] - Fixed several instances where the player was able to get stuck in the map (Collisions).
- [Fixes] - Several textures have been increased in resolution.
- [Fixes] - Slightly decreased the player footstep volume.
- [Fixes] - Spelling and grammar errors.

Let me end this off by once again thanking you all for supporting this game and its development. I am very happy to see that many of you enjoy Inside Depth 6 and what is has to offer. As always, I will do my best to improve my craft, and create and even better game to come! 

Cheers, everybody. And happy gaming!

Stan.T

notes.title: Ever wonder what Inside Depth 6 looks like?
notes.content:
Have you ever wondered what Inside Depth 6 actually looks like from a distance? Well here you have it! a visual of Inside Depth 6; its size, and all of its glory.

You will also notice a new area called [b]Hell Hole[/b]. This has not yet been released, and it also has not yet been fully developed, so its actual size will be a bit bigger than is currently shown in the picture.

When developing Inside Depth 6, I had one goal in mind. My goal was not to scare the player as much as possible, it was not to throw countless jump scares at you, rather, my goal was to create a journey for the player to experience. Every depth has a unique layout, differing assets, interactions, and even the stone on the walls are different to represent a descent to the lower realms of the earth's crust.

There are countless of indie horror games on the market right now which isolate the player in a single room, house, and environment to the point where adventure and journeying becomes non-existent. I am not saying this is a bad thing, rather, I was a little tired of it and wanted to try something completely new that I have never done before. And so, this is how Inside Depth 6 was born! Replayability was also a big concern for me. To combat this, I have added multiple routs to descend the mines, multiple endings, and now with Version 2's Hell Hole, there will be yet another path to take to bring you closer to the sixth depth. This approach creates a whole new experience when playing the game for a second or even a third time.

Of course, my next game, however, may go back to my traditional roots of scale because I feel that I can create a far more terrifying, immersive experience if I sacrifice some scale. Though, I can promise you that my next game will definitely be a new experience, to say the least.

As for Inside Depth 6's [b]upcoming Version 2.0 update[/b], I will be sure to post more information on this near the end of this month (April).

Cheers, everybody! Stay safe out there and happy gaming.

Stan. T

notes.title: Inside Depth 6 is fast approaching!
notes.content:
[b]Hello, everybody; I hope you are all safe, well, and prepared for Inside Depth 6!
[/b]
I wanted to let you all know that Depth 6 less than 24 hours away from release date, and that it is officially 100% complete and ready for some gameplays!

I am very excited to see as many gameplays as I can, to see your reactions, and to see which paths you end up taking. Inside Depth 6 offers many mysteries and secrets to solve alongside a dark and mysterious storyline. Be sure to keep a watchful eye for items to interact with, and hidden paths to uncover or explore.

[b]As always, as with any horror game, here are some fine practices to get the most out of Inside Depth 6:[/b]
- Use earphones or headphones while Playing Inside Depth 6,
- Be sure to crank the volume up to a reasonable amount to immerse yourself into all of the 3D audio,
- Play alone and in the dark if possible,
- and definitely full-screen the game for that nice cinema experience :)

For all of the ultra high-end computers out there, if you are pumping out 61 or more FPS, consider enabling V-SYNC in settings to keep your GPU nice and cool and to prevent any screen tearing/jittering. An FPS option is also available in options if you like keeping an eye on your FPS. Plus, it looks cool, regardless, on the left side of the camera interface (a win - win) :)

I look forward to watching your gameplays and reading your reviews for Inside Depth 6, so please, if you are able, leave a review of the game once you have finished the game. All reviews help me gage the audience interest, they help me uncover areas of the game that may require some improvement, or areas of the game that you consider amazing! All of this information is always put to good use in the next upcoming game.

[b]As for upcoming games[/b], my next goal is to get better at game development. In other words, I will be spending a few weeks learning new methods of code, touching VR, and learning how to achieve better, more realistic graphics / visuals while maintaining an optimized game. Of course, I hope to add new mechanics, new systems, and new ways to engage the player. Time will tell what happens next, but I have high hopes going forward. 

[b]Cheers, everybody, and please stay safe!
[/b]
[i][b]Depth 6 will be released on March 12, 10:00 AM PST and 11:00 AM Mountain Time[/b][/i]

notes.title: Inside Depth 6 is coming soon!
notes.content:
[b]Hello everyone, I hope you are all doing well.
[/b]
I wanted to let everyone here know that [u][b]Inside Depth 6's Steam page is now LIVE![/b][/u]  After many months of development, I am very happy to say that the game is almost finished and ready to provide you all with some long awaited spooks.

I have learned a lot from Suite 776 and lots of the feedback received. I have taking this feedback very seriously and have applied the following to Inside Depth 6:
- Multiple endings,
- A random variant system (some events will trigger differently for everybody),
- Longer gameplay and a stronger focus on story,
- Significantly more exploration relative to Suite 776,
- More secrets and optional puzzles to take part in,
- and of course, an Easter egg; who doesn't love a little bit of Easter egg love?

[b]So what are my plans once Inside Depth 6 is released?[/b]
Once Inside Depth 6 is fully live, I intend to push out a couple of updates to the game within 1-2 months time. This is to scrub a couple of triggers, add a couple of additional areas to explore and a few additional scares.

Most of my time after launch will be focused on research. Due to Covid, I am focusing full time on Game development and Youtube, so this will allow me to focus on researching areas of game development like advanced AI, animations, and most importantly, for me, it gives me time to finally look into virtual reality (VR). It has been a long-awaited dream of mine to delve into some VR development, so now with all of this extra time to focus on game dev, I can allocate a lot of resources to VR research, And who knows, maybe I will be able to add VR support to Inside Depth 6 and Suite 776 within the next several months.

Another area of importance for me is to research controller support and localization. I know that controller support and a lack of additional languages is a major negative to my titles, so I hope to implement some form of controller support and localization in the future - please bear with me on that! :)

So as always, I wish you all a safe and enjoyable 2021, happy gaming, stay safe, and I look forward to hearing from you all once Inside Depth 6 has been released March 12!

Please feel free to provide some of your thoughts in the comments below :)
